name: schtasks.exe
description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.
summary: Created a scheduled SYSTEM task that runs when a user logs in
Run malicious scripts on a compromised host (.vbe, .dat)
Downloaded additional malware including Cobalt Strike, PowerShell loader

associated_apts.name: APT3
associated_apts.description: An APT3 downloader creates persistence by creating the following scheduled task: schtasks /create /tn "mysc" /tr C:\Users\Public\test.exe /sc ONLOGON /ru "System".

associated_apts.name: BianLian Ransomware Group
associated_apts.evidence: reported by CISA AA23-136A BianLian Ransomware Group May 2023
associated_apts.description: BianLian group actors used a Scheduled Task run as SYSTEM (the highest privilege Windows accounts) to execute a Dynamic Link Library (DLL) file daily. schtasks.exe /RU SYSTEM /create /sc ONCE /<user> /tr "cmd.exe /crundll32.exe c:\programdata\netsh.dll,Entry" /ST 04:43
associated_apts.sources: CISA AA23-136A BianLian Ransomware Group May 2023 https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-136a

associated_apts.name: BlackCat Ransomware Actors & Affiliates
associated_apts.evidence: reported by Cisco Talos BlackMatter to BlackCat March 2022
associated_apts.description: During the BlackCat attack, the actors used a tool called [reverse-ssh] ... c:\windows\system32\schtasks.exe /create /ru system /sc minute /tn microsoft\windows\wininet\cachetask /tr c:\:cachetask -b <bind port> /f

associated_campaigns.name: C0017
associated_campaigns.description: During C0017, APT41 used `SCHTASKS /Change` to modify legitimate scheduled tasks to run malicious code.

associated_campaigns.name: Operation CuckooBees
associated_campaigns.description: During Operation CuckooBees, the threat actors used scheduled tasks to execute batch scripts for lateral movement with the following command: `SCHTASKS /Create /S <IP Address> /U <Username> /p <Password> /SC ONCE /TN test /TR <Path to a Batch File> /ST <Time> /RU SYSTEM.`

associated_campaigns.name: SolarWinds Compromise
associated_campaigns.description: During the SolarWinds Compromise, APT29 used `scheduler` and `schtasks` to create new tasks on remote host as part of their lateral movement. They manipulated scheduled tasks by updating an existing legitimate task to execute their tools and then returned the scheduled task to its original configuration. APT29 also created a scheduled task to maintain SUNSPOT persistence when the host booted.
associated_campaigns.sources: Volexity SolarWinds https://www.volexity.com/blog/2020/12/14/dark-halo-leverages-solarwinds-compromise-to-breach-organizations/; CrowdStrike SUNSPOT Implant January 2021 https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/sunspot-malware-technical-analysis/; FireEye SUNBURST Backdoor December 2020 https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2020/12/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor.html

associated_malware.name: The Gentlemen Ransomware
associated_malware.description: The Gentlemen Ransomware has leveraged scheduled tasks to execute itself as system. related_CVE.description: Windows Task Scheduler elevation of privilege. The public proof of concept runs a legacy Windows XP schtasks.exe (/change /TN bear /RU /RP) against a hard-linked task file to take over a protected file; this is a public exploit, not a documented intrusion.

Netlogon (MS-NRPC) elevation of privilege, known as Zerologon. In a Qbot intrusion where the actors exploited it to get domain admin, Qbot used schtasks.exe to create a task that ran every 30 minutes for persistence.
